top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, one writer in one prize part) is the only proposal that names a writer, and my literary judgment supports it independently of the six-way convergence, which I do not count as merit. The voice is recognisable within a few sentences. Public knowledge of the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid places them among large, deliberately patterned structures in which memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation form one world, and the sentence as well as the scale carries that ambition. The oeuvre appears to run from poetry through early prose to the major cycles, which supports a whole-oeuvre citation grounded in a poet's language and not in poetry as a co-equal pillar. Real reservations remain: I judge the Romanian only through translations of uneven quality, I cannot confirm volume by volume that later books extend rather than repeat earlier motifs, the poetry is the thinnest strand in my evidence, and I have not independently verified any source. None of these is substantiated against the work, and the alternatives I raised (Can Xue, NDiaye) are less well evidenced for me, not demonstrably stronger. P000 ranks second because it is the only remaining option and is a weaker outcome than awarding a writer whose merit I consider established on the available evidence.
